newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S. soldier jailed for murder in South Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldier jailed for murder in South Korea.

text.p: A South Korean court sentenced a U.S. serviceman to 15 years in jail on Thursday after convicting him of murdering a Korean prostitute, a court official said.

It was not clear whether Private Eric Munnich from Chicago will appeal against the sentence. During his trial he confessed to stabbing to death the prostitute in a drunken rage during a quarrel over payment.
Prosecutors had demanded life in jail for Munnich, whose trial sparked renewed public protests in South Korea over the presence of 37,000 U.S. troops in the country.

The judge at the Seoul District Criminal Court explained he had handed down a lesser sentence because Munnich was drunk at the time of the killing and emotionally unstable as a new arrival in South Korea, the official said.
The body of Lee Ki-sun, 44, was discovered in a boarding house near a U.S. military base north of Seoul in September.
U.S. forces are stationed in South Korea to deter aggression from North Korea. The two Koreas have been technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.
